1	# Key Data Flows
     2	
     3	## 1. Full Build Pipeline (`build()`)
     4	
     5	The main `build(config)` entry point orchestrates the entire pipeline:
     6	
     7	```
     8	build(config)
     9	  │
    10	  ├─ Pre-scan: buildAgentNameMap(config)
    11	  │     │
    12	  │     ├─ For each suite in config.suites:
    13	  │     │     ├─ Load _shared.yaml → default_version fallback
    14	  │     │     ├─ Discover persona YAML files
    15	  │     │     └─ For each persona:
    16	  │     │           key   = "agent_" + slug (hyphens → underscores)     → "<name> v<version>"
    17	  │     │           key   = "agent_slug_" + slug (hyphens → underscores) → slug (hyphens preserved)
    18	  │     └─ Return agentMap: Record<string, string>
    19	  │
    20	  ├─ For each suite in config.suites:
    21	  │     │
    22	  │     ├─ buildSuite(suiteName, suiteConfig, config, plugins, agentMap)
    23	  │     │     │
    24	  │     │     ├─ Load _shared.yaml → sharedMeta
    25	  │     │     ├─ Load partials (BuildConfig.partials → shared → suite-local overlay) → partialsMap
    26	  │     │     ├─ Run onSuiteInit hooks on all plugins
    27	  │     │     ├─ Run onPartials hooks on all plugins (accumulating partialsMap)
    28	  │     │     ├─ Discover persona YAML files (meta/*.yaml, excluding _*.yaml)
    29	  │     │     │
    30	  │     │     └─ For each persona × each target:
    31	  │     │           │
    32	  │     │           └─ buildPersona(yamlPath, …, target, agentMap)
    33	  │     │                 │
    34	  │     │                 ├─ 1. Load persona YAML → personaMeta
    35	  │     │                 ├─ 2. Merge context (BuildConfig.variables → SuiteConfig.variables →
    36	  │     │                 │      sharedMeta → personaMeta → derived fields → agentMap → target flags)
    37	  │     │                 ├─ 3. Run onBuildContext hooks (context accumulation)
    38	  │     │                 ├─ 4. Run onPersonaPartials hooks (per-persona partials accumulation;
    39	                 │      a shallow copy of partialsMap is created before the first hook
    40	                 │      so that persona-level overrides are isolated per persona)
    41	  │     │                 ├─ 5. Resolve frontmatter template (plugin → config → default)
    42	  │     │                 ├─ 6. Render frontmatter (conditionals → variables)
    43	  │     │                 ├─ 7. Load content template (.md file)
    44	  │     │                 ├─ 8. Render body:
    45	  │     │                 │     ├─ resolvePartials (depth-2 recursion)
    46	  │     │                 │     ├─ resolveConditionals
    47	  │     │                 │     ├─ resolveVariables
    48	  │     │                 │     ├─ collapseBlankLines
    49	  │     │                 │     └─ ensureBlankLineBeforeHeadings
    50	  │     │                 ├─ 9. Assemble output (frontmatter + body)
    51	  │     │                 ├─ 10. Run onPostRender hooks (output chain)
    52	  │     │                 ├─ 11. Run onValidate hooks (collect ValidationResults)
    53	  │     │                 ├─ 12. Determine output path (vs_file_name / cc_file_name)
    54	  │     │                 └─ 13. Write file (unless check mode)
    55	  │     │
    56	  │     └─ Collect BuildResult[]
    57	  │
    58	  ├─ Aggregate results → BuildSummary
    59	  ├─ If strict: check for error/warning ValidationResults → strictFailures
    60	  └─ Return BuildSummary
    61	```
    62	
    63	## 2. Context Merge Order
    64	
    65	Template variables are resolved from a merged context object. Later values win:
    66	
    67	```
    68	0.   BuildConfig.variables       (global defaults — lowest priority)
    69	   ↓ overridden by
    70	0.5. SuiteConfig.variables       (suite-level defaults)
    71	   ↓ overridden by
    72	1. _shared.yaml defaults         (suite-level base)
    73	   ↓ overridden by
    74	2. Per-persona YAML fields       (persona-specific values)
    75	   ↓ augmented by
    76	3. Derived convenience fields    (version, tools_list, cc_file_name_stem, etc.)
    77	   ↓ augmented by
    78	4. Cross-suite agent name map    (agent_* keys, only when not already present)
    79	   ↓ augmented by
    80	5. Plugin onBuildContext hooks    (each plugin mutates/extends context)
    81	```
    82	
    83	### Derived Fields (auto-computed)
    84	
    85	| Field | Source | Condition |
    86	|-------|--------|-----------|
    87	| `version` | `personaMeta.version` → `sharedMeta.default_version` → `'0.0.0'` | Always |
    88	| `tools_list` | `serializeToolsList(tools)` | Always |
    89	| `tools_json` | `serializeTools(tools)` | Always |
    90	| `cc_tools_list` | `serializeToolsList(cc_tools ?? tools)` | Always |
    91	| `cc_tools_json` | `serializeTools(cc_tools ?? tools)` | Always |
    92	| `cc_file_name_stem` | `cc_file_name` with `.md` extension stripped | Always |
    93	| `da_file_name_stem` | `da_file_name` with `.md` extension stripped | Only when `da_file_name` is set |
    94	| `da_tools_list` | `serializeToolsList(da_tools ?? tools)` | Only when `da_file_name` is set |
    95	| `da_tools_json` | `serializeTools(da_tools ?? tools)` | Only when `da_file_name` is set |
    96	| `agent_<slug>` | `"<name> v<version>"` for every persona across all suites; slug hyphens → underscores in key | Always |
    97	| `agent_slug_<slug>` | Raw hyphenated slug string for every persona; key uses underscores, value preserves hyphens | Always |
    98	
    99	Derived fields are only set when not already present in the merged context — explicit YAML values always win.
   100

1	# Public API Surface
     2	
     3	All public symbols are exported from the package entry point `@mistralys/persona-builder` (via `src/index.ts`).
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Constants
     8	
     9	### `VERSION`
    10	
    11	```ts
    12	export const VERSION: string;
    13	```
    14	
    15	Package version string sourced from `package.json` at runtime via `createRequire`.
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## Top-Level Functions
    20	
    21	### `build(config)`
    22	
    23	```ts
    24	export async function build(config: BuildConfig): Promise<BuildSummary>;
    25	```
    26	
    27	Main entry point. Pre-scans all suites to build a cross-suite agent name map (`agent_*` display-name variables and `agent_slug_*` raw-slug variables), then iterates all suites × targets, orchestrates the full pipeline (discover → load → render → validate → write), and returns an aggregated summary. Respects `check` (no writes) and `strict` (fail on warnings/errors) flags.
    28	
    29	### `buildSuite(suiteName, suiteConfig, config, plugins, target, agentMap?, registry?)`
    30	
    31	```ts
    32	export async function buildSuite(
    33	  suiteName: string,
    34	  suiteConfig: SuiteConfig,
    35	  config: BuildConfig,
    36	  plugins: PersonaBuildPlugin[],
    37	  target: string,
    38	  agentMap?: Record<string, string>,
    39	  registry?: TargetRegistry,
    40	): Promise<BuildResult[]>;
    41	```
    42	
    43	Builds all personas in a single suite for a single target. Loads `_shared.yaml`, merges partials, fires `onSuiteInit` and `onPartials` hooks, discovers persona YAMLs, and delegates to `buildPersona()`. The optional `agentMap` is forwarded to each persona build.
    44	
    45	**Two-registry limitation:** `registry` defaults to `defaultRegistry`. If you pass a custom `TargetRegistry` only to `build()` (via `config.targetRegistry`) and call `buildSuite()` directly without the same registry argument, your custom targets will not be visible. Either pass the registry instance explicitly here, or use `build()` to have it forwarded automatically.
    46	
    47	### `buildPersona(personaYamlPath, suiteName, suiteConfig, sharedMeta, partialsMap, config, plugins, target, agentMap?, registry?)`
    48	
    49	```ts
    50	export async function buildPersona(
    51	  personaYamlPath: string,
    52	  suiteName: string,
    53	  suiteConfig: SuiteConfig,
    54	  sharedMeta: Record<string, unknown>,
    55	  partialsMap: Record<string, string>,
    56	  config: BuildConfig,
    57	  plugins: PersonaBuildPlugin[],
    58	  target: string,
    59	  agentMap?: Record<string, string>,
    60	  registry?: TargetRegistry,
    61	): Promise<BuildResult>;
    62	```
    63	
    64	Builds a single persona for a single target. Runs the full rendering pipeline: load metadata → build context (`onBuildContext`) → per-persona partials (`onPersonaPartials`) → frontmatter → body rendering → post-processing (`onPostRender`) → validation (`onValidate`) → write.
    65	
    66	**Two-registry limitation:** `registry` defaults to `defaultRegistry`. If you pass a custom `TargetRegistry` only to `build()` (via `config.targetRegistry`) and call `buildPersona()` directly without the same registry argument, your custom targets will not be visible. Either pass the registry instance explicitly here, or use `build()` to have it forwarded automatically.
    67	
    68	---
    69	
    70	## Cross-Suite Template Context Variables
    71	
    72	Populated by `buildAgentNameMap()` during the pre-scan phase of `build()`. For every persona across all configured suites, two context keys are injected:
    73	
    74	| Key pattern | Value | Typical use |
    75	|-------------|-------|-------------|
    76	| `agent_<underscored_slug>` | `"<name> v<version>"` | Reference another persona by display name in template prose, e.g. `{{agent_my_persona}}` renders as `"My Persona v1.0.0"`. |
    77	| `agent_slug_<underscored_slug>` | Raw hyphenated slug string | Invoke another persona as a subagent in templates, e.g. `task(subagent={{agent_slug_my_persona}})` renders as `task(subagent=my-persona)`. Useful with the Deep Agents target. |
    78	
    79	**Key derivation:** The YAML `slug` field (falling back to the filename stem when absent) is transformed for the key suffix: hyphens replaced with underscores. The *value* of `agent_slug_*` keys preserves the original hyphens, since subagent names use hyphenated slugs.
    80	
    81	**Example** — a persona with `slug: my-great-agent` produces:
    82	- `agent_my_great_agent` → `"My Great Agent v1.2.0"`
    83	- `agent_slug_my_great_agent` → `"my-great-agent"`
    84	
    85	Both keys are injected at context merge step 4 (after derived fields, before plugin hooks) and are only set when not already present — explicit YAML overrides always win. See **Context Merge Order** in `data-flows.md`.
    86	
    87	---
    88	## Derived Context Fields
    89	
    90	Fields computed by `buildContext()` at build time (merge step 3). All are only set when not already present — YAML overrides always win.
    91	
    92	### Standard Derived Fields (always injected)
    93	
    94	| Field | Derived from | Format |
    95	|-------|-------------|--------|
    96	| `version` | `version` → `default_version` → `'0.0.0'` | String |
    97	| `tools_list` | `tools` array | `'tool1', 'tool2'` |
    98	| `tools_json` | `tools` array | `['tool1', 'tool2']` |
    99	| `cc_tools_list` | `cc_tools` → fallback to `tools` | `'tool1', 'tool2'` |
   100	| `cc_tools_json` | `cc_tools` → fallback to `tools` | `['tool1', 'tool2']` |

101	> **`da_*` gate:** The `da_file_name_stem`, `da_tools_list`, and `da_tools_json` fields are
   102	> gated on `da_file_name` being present in the merged context. Personas without `da_file_name`
   103	> will not have these fields injected (no error, no empty string). This differs from the
   104	> `cc_*` equivalents which are always emitted unconditionally.
   105	
   106	## 3. Frontmatter Template Precedence
   107	
   108	```
   109	Plugin frontmatterTemplates     (first registered plugin with target key wins)
   110	   ↓ fallback
   111	BuildConfig.frontmatter         (config-level override)
   112	   ↓ fallback
   113	Library defaults                (DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_VSCODE / DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_CLAUDE_CODE)
   114	```
   115	
   116	## 4. Partials Resolution
   117	
   118	```
   119	0. BuildConfig.partials          (inline map — lowest priority)
   120	   ↓ overlaid by
   121	1. Shared partials dir (sharedPartialsDir)
   122	   ↓ overlaid by (suite-local overrides shared on name collision)
   123	2. Suite-local partials dir (srcDir/partials/)
   124	   ↓ result: Combined partialsMap passed to plugin hooks
   125	3. onPartials hooks              (runPartials — once per suite, after step 2; highest suite-level priority)
   126	   ↓ result: Suite-level partialsMap (shallow-copied per persona before step 4)
   127	4. onPersonaPartials hooks       (runPersonaPartials — per persona × target, after onBuildContext)
   128	   ↓ result: Persona-scoped partialsMap (isolated per persona)
   129	5. resolvePartials(template, partialsMap)  ← depth-2 recursion
   130	```
   131	
   132	## 5. Plugin Hook Execution Order
   133	
   134	Per persona, hooks fire in this order:
   135	
   136	```
   137	1. onSuiteInit(suite, sharedMeta)                          ← once per suite (before any persona)
   138	2. onPartials(partialsMap, suiteName, suite)                ← once per suite (after partials loaded)
   139	3. onBuildContext(context, persona, suite)                  ← per persona, before rendering
   140	4. onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona, context, suite)  ← per persona, before rendering (after onBuildContext)
   141	5. onPostRender(output, persona, target)                    ← per persona, after rendering
   142	6. onValidate(persona, suite, target?)                      ← per persona, after post-render
   143	```
   144	
   145	Within each hook, plugins are invoked in **registration order** (array index in `config.plugins`).
   146	
   147	- `onBuildContext`, `onPartials`, `onPersonaPartials`, and `onPostRender` are **accumulating** — each plugin receives the prior plugin's output.
   148	- `onValidate` is **collecting** — results are concatenated into a flat array.
   149	
   150	## 6. CLI Flow
   151	
   152	```
   153	persona-build [flags]
   154	  │
   155	  ├─ Parse args (--config, --check, --strict, --help, --version)
   156	  ├─ Load config file (dynamic import: .js ESM / .cjs / .json)
   157	  ├─ Merge CLI flags into BuildConfig
   158	  ├─ Call build(config)
   159	  ├─ Report results to stdout
   160	  └─ Exit code: 0 (success) or 1 (strict failure)
   161	```
   162	
   163	## 7. Output File Naming
   164	
   165	```
   166	For each persona × target:
   167	  1. Check context[filenameContextKey]:
   168	       VS Code target      → context['vs_file_name']
   169	       Claude Code target  → context['cc_file_name']
   170	       Deep Agents target  → context['da_file_name']
   171	       Custom target       → context[TargetDefinition.filenameContextKey] (if defined)
   172	  2. If present → use as the output basename
   173	  3. If absent  → fall back to content filename (persona-name.md)
   174	  4. Output path = outputDir / basename
   175	```

101	| `cc_file_name_stem` | `cc_file_name` with `.md` stripped | String |
   102	
   103	### Deep Agents Derived Fields (gated on `da_file_name` presence)
   104	
   105	These three fields mirror the `cc_*` pattern but apply to the `deep-agents` target. They are **only injected when `da_file_name` is present** in the merged context — personas without `da_file_name` produce no `da_*` fields and no error.
   106	
   107	| Field | Derived from | Format |
   108	|-------|-------------|--------|
   109	| `da_file_name_stem` | `da_file_name` with `.md` stripped | String |
   110	| `da_tools_list` | `da_tools` → fallback to `tools` | `'tool1', 'tool2'` |
   111	| `da_tools_json` | `da_tools` → fallback to `tools` | `['tool1', 'tool2']` |
   112	
   113	**`da_*` gate asymmetry vs `cc_*`:** The `cc_*` tools fields are emitted unconditionally for all personas, but the `da_*` fields are gated on `da_file_name` being set. This means personas that do not produce a Deep Agents output file will never have `da_*` in their context, rather than receiving empty values.
   114	
   115	---
   116	## Engine Functions
   117	
   118	All engine functions are **pure** — zero imports, no side effects, no file I/O.
   119	
   120	### `resolvePartials(text, partialsMap, depth?)`
   121	
   122	```ts
   123	export function resolvePartials(
   124	  text: string,
   125	  partialsMap: Record<string, string>,
   126	  depth?: number,
   127	): string;
   128	```
   129	
   130	Replaces `{{> name}}` markers with content from `partialsMap`. Recursion capped at depth 2. Missing partials emit `console.warn` and are preserved as-is.
   131	
   132	### `resolveConditionals(text, context)`
   133	
   134	```ts
   135	export function resolveConditionals(
   136	  text: string,
   137	  context: Record<string, unknown>,
   138	): string;
   139	```
   140	
   141	Evaluates `{{#if flag}}…{{/if}}`, `{{#if flag}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}`, and `{{#if flag}}…{{else if flag2}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}` (chain) blocks.
   142	
   143	`{{else if}}` chains are pre-processed by `resolveElseIf()` (internal), which rewrites each innermost `{{else if flag}}` segment into an equivalent `{{else}}{{#if flag}}` nested block before the main resolution pass. Multi-level chains are unwound iteratively — one level per pass — until the string stabilises.
   144	
   145	Nested `{{#if}}` blocks inside `{{else}}` branches are supported — resolved innermost-first across multiple passes until stable. `{{else if}}` chains may be freely mixed with traditional nested syntax. Unknown flags treated as falsy.
   146	
   147	### `resolveVariables(text, context, filename)`
   148	
   149	```ts
   150	export function resolveVariables(
   151	  text: string,
   152	  context: Record<string, unknown>,
   153	  filename: string,
   154	): string;
   155	```
   156	
   157	Substitutes `{{varName}}` tokens with `String(context[varName])`. Unresolved variables emit `console.warn` and are preserved.
   158	
   159	### `collapseBlankLines(text)`
   160	
   161	```ts
   162	export function collapseBlankLines(text: string): string;
   163	```
   164	
   165	Collapses 3+ consecutive blank lines into 2.
   166	
   167	### `ensureBlankLineBeforeHeadings(text)`
   168	
   169	```ts
   170	export function ensureBlankLineBeforeHeadings(text: string): string;
   171	```
   172	
   173	Inserts a blank line before Markdown headings and horizontal rules when missing.
   174	
   175	### `normalizeNewlines(text)`
   176	
   177	```ts
   178	export function normalizeNewlines(text: string): string;
   179	```
   180	
   181	Converts CRLF/CR to LF.
   182	
   183	### `serializeTools(tools)`
   184	
   185	```ts
   186	export function serializeTools(tools: string[]): string;
   187	```
   188	
   189	Returns YAML flow-sequence with outer brackets: `['tool1', 'tool2']`.
   190	
   191	### `serializeToolsList(tools)`
   192	
   193	```ts
   194	export function serializeToolsList(tools: string[]): string;
   195	```
   196	
   197	Returns comma-separated quoted tool names without brackets: `'tool1', 'tool2'`.
   198	
   199	---

201	## Loader Functions
   202	
   203	All loaders perform async file I/O via `node:fs/promises`.
   204	
   205	### `loadPartials(dir)`
   206	
   207	```ts
   208	export async function loadPartials(dir: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
   209	```
   210	
   211	Reads all `.md` files in `dir` and returns a map from filename stem to content string.
   212	
   213	### `discoverPersonaYamls(root)`
   214	
   215	```ts
   216	export async function discoverPersonaYamls(root: string): Promise<string[]>;
   217	```
   218	
   219	Recursively discovers all `*.yaml` files under `root`. Returns sorted absolute paths. Uses `readdir({ recursive: true })` (Node ≥ 18.17).
   220	
   221	### `loadMetadata(yamlPath)`
   222	
   223	```ts
   224	export async function loadMetadata(yamlPath: string): Promise<PersonaMetadata>;
   225	```
   226	
   227	Parses a YAML file into a typed `PersonaMetadata` object. Throws if the file is not a valid object or is missing the required `name` field.
   228	
   229	### `loadContent(mdPath)`
   230	
   231	```ts
   232	export async function loadContent(mdPath: string): Promise<string>;
   233	```
   234	
   235	Reads a Markdown content template as a raw UTF-8 string. No parsing or template resolution.
   236	
   237	---
   238	
   239	## Utility Functions
   240	
   241	### `escapeRegExp(str)`
   242	
   243	```ts
   244	export function escapeRegExp(str: string): string;
   245	```
   246	
   247	Escapes all regex special characters in `str` for safe use inside a `new RegExp(...)` constructor. Pure function — no I/O, no side effects.
   248	
   249	---
   250	
   251	## Validator Functions
   252	
   253	Both validators are pure functions — no I/O, no side effects.
   254	
   255	### `validateFileName(filePath)`
   256	
   257	```ts
   258	export function validateFileName(filePath: string): ValidationResult[];
   259	```
   260	
   261	Validates a filename against kebab-case naming convention. Returns one `ValidationResult` (severity `'error'`) per violated rule. Rules: no uppercase, no spaces, kebab-case segments only.
   262	
   263	### `validateStrictMarkers(renderedContent, requiredMarkers)`
   264	
   265	```ts
   266	export function validateStrictMarkers(
   267	  renderedContent: string,
   268	  requiredMarkers: string[],
   269	): ValidationResult[];
   270	```
   271	
   272	Checks that every marker in `requiredMarkers` appears verbatim in `renderedContent`. Returns one error per missing marker.
   273	
   274	---
   275	
   276	## Frontmatter Functions
   277	
   278	### `resolveFrontmatterTemplate(target, plugins, configTemplates?)`
   279	
   280	```ts
   281	export function resolveFrontmatterTemplate(
   282	  target: string,
   283	  plugins: PersonaBuildPlugin[],
   284	  configTemplates?: Record<string, string>,
   285	): string;
   286	```
   287	
   288	Resolves the frontmatter template for a target. Precedence: plugin `frontmatterTemplates` (first plugin wins) → config-level templates → library defaults. For custom target names (neither `'vscode'` nor `'claude-code'`), the library-default fallback returns the Claude Code template unless overridden via a plugin or `configTemplates`.
   289	
   290	### `renderFrontmatter(template, context, filename)`
   291	
   292	```ts
   293	export function renderFrontmatter(
   294	  template: string,
   295	  context: Record<string, unknown>,

   366	### `TargetRegistry`
   367	
   368	```ts
   369	export class TargetRegistry {
   370	  register(definition: TargetDefinition): void;

   372	  has(name: string): boolean;

   374	  allDefinitions(): TargetDefinition[];
